note: G-125 is an OPS-17 row on hauska-engine + hauska-map, not an OPS-23 row. scripts/surface-probe.mjs is scoped to OPS-23's specific parcel set and facet-parity predicates against smartsite.cloud/cortex; it has no G-125 predicate and its infrastructure does not carry a paid/authenticated PE session, which the flood-drainage report requires. Rather than force a mismatched fit into that shared script (touching a heavily-used file many concurrent lanes depend on, for a predicate it was never built to express), this is a HAND-WRITTEN probe in the same spirit: every claim below is a live measurement against the actually-deployed production surface, not an inference from a merged PR, a local test, or a store read, exactly per R-4's own standard ('a merged PR ... alone never closes a lane').

hauska-engine-api.verifiedBy: gcloud run services update-traffic ... describe, read by field name post-shift

property-explorer.verifiedBy: vercel deploy --prod output (readyState READY, target production, Aliased https://smartsite.cloud)

predicates.falsifier: rainfallDepthInches/rainfallSource in the response stay pinned at the default regardless of the parameter, or no downstream stat/text changes at all
predicates.method: Two live authenticated POST /v1/property-nodes/48021:34049/flood-drainage/refresh calls against the deployed engine-api canary (pre-shift, same image now serving 100%), real Bastrop parcel 48021:34049, real USGS 3DEP DEM fetch, real pysheds computation (computation.library: 'pysheds', not the native fallback)
predicates.verdict: PASS -- materially different result: on-parcel ponding roughly halved, region-wide ponding to about 30 percent, at a real depth change on a real parcel

predicates.falsifier: a parameter-sourced run's gradient note or PDF Design-storm line claims '100-yr' without a curve backing that claim
predicates.method: Read gradient.note verbatim from the live response
predicates.firstLiveRunFound: Design storm 4 inch, 100-yr 24-hr. -- FAIL, a real bug the first deploy shipped
predicates.afterFixRedeployVerified: Design storm 4 inch, 24-hr. -- PASS, no fabricated year claim
verifiedOn: canary tag URL (hauska-engine-api-00224-joq via g125-fix tag)
predicates.verdict: PASS after the follow-up fix (PR #447); FAIL on the first deploy (PR #446 alone) -- recorded here rather than smoothed over

predicates.falsifier: the no-param request produces a different rainfallDepthInches/rainfallSource than the pre-G-125 code would have, for reasons other than the pre-existing NOAA-parser defect
predicates.result: rainfallSource resolved to 'default' (9.5in), matching pre-G-125 behavior exactly for a live NOAA-fetch failure -- the ONLY new field is the additive, absent-when-unavailable rainfallCurve

predicates.falsifier: the deployed property-explorer JS bundle does not contain the new depth control, honesty disclaimer, or the components mount hidden behind the embed flag
predicates.method: curl the live smartsite.cloud bundle post-deploy, grep for the new testids/copy verbatim
predicates.result: flood-depth-control:1 flood-honesty-disclaimer:2 'Screening-level drainage model':1 flood-run-at-depth:1 flood-depth-presets:1 'Run at this depth':1 -- all present in the served bundle

predicates.falsifier: a custom-depth refresh is systematically slower than a default refresh on the same code path, supporting the dispatch's premise that async/polling infra is needed specifically for this control
predicates.method: Compare wall-clock across 3 live calls on 2 revisions: revision A's FIRST call (default, 102.8s) vs revision A's SECOND call (param 4in, same warm container, 12.0s) vs revision B's FIRST call (param 4in, fresh container, 92.5s)
predicates.result: The FIRST call to a fresh container was slow REGARDLESS of depth (102.8s default, 92.5s param) while a SECOND call to an already-warm container was fast (12.0s) -- container cold-start (subprocess spawn, native GDAL/pysheds import cost per hydrologyWorkerClient.ts's per-request `spawn(python3, ...)`), not the rainfall depth, is the dominant latency driver. No code-level differential exists: both paths run the identical DEM fetch + pysheds call; the parameter path additionally now awaits the same concurrent NOAA fetch the default path already paid.
predicates.decision: No new async-refresh/polling infrastructure built for this control (see CP1/CP2 for the full reasoning and the distinction from the unrelated P-155 feasibility-timeout program, which already owns that problem for a different report).
predicates.verdict: PASS -- falsifier not observed; risk is pre-existing and not depth-differential

leaveBehindConfirmedLive: The live NOAA HDSC endpoint (https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/new/cgi_readH5.py) returns a JavaScript array-literal payload (quantiles=[[...]]), not the <tr><td> HTML table packages/adapters/src/hydrology/noaaAtlas14.ts's parsePfdsDepthTable expects (confirmed by a direct curl of the real endpoint AND by every live production run in this probe returning rainfallSource:'default'/rainfallCurve:absent for the no-param path). This is pre-existing, out of G-125's scope, and affects every county, not just Bastrop -- named precisely for the operator, not fixed here.
